title: Ram Chandra v. State of U.P. — OTS proposal not a recovery certificate; pending 6.5 objection
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.; Vikram D. Chauhan, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; OTS proposal not quashed; liberty to press pending 6.5 objection.
headnote: An OTS proposal offering waiver of surcharge is not a recovery certificate and will not be quashed in writ. A consumer previously relegated to Clauses 5.6 and 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, after a defective meter with a broken seal, must press any pending objection under those clauses rather than obtain quashing of the OTS communication.
facts: Ram Chandra, a 1 kVA consumer occupying a kachcha house, sought quashing of a 30 September 2021 demand of Rs 1,07,497.07, described as a recovery certificate. An 18 September 2021 citation had claimed Rs 67,261. The meter was found defective with the seal broken. An earlier writ (Writ-C No. 6084 of 2020) was disposed of on 20 February 2020 with liberty to invoke Clauses 5.6 and 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. He claimed a 2 March 2020 objection but produced no decision.

holding_units.topic: pending billing objection after OTS proposal misdescribed as recovery
holding_units.holding: Where a consumer, already given liberty to invoke Clauses 5.6 and 6.5 after a defective-meter demand, seeks to quash a later communication as a recovery certificate, the Court will not quash it if the document is only an OTS proposal offering surcharge waiver. The writ is disposed of with liberty to press the pending Clause 6.5 (and 5.6) objection if it remains undecided.

principle_tags.application: The prayer to quash the alleged recovery was refused on the footing that the paper was an OTS proposal; the consumer was left to press a pending Clause 6.5 objection instead of a merits decision on the dues.
The petitioner claimed a 2 March 2020 objection pursuant to an earlier 5.6/6.5 liberty order; the Court remitted him to press that objection if still undecided.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the electricity dues and the pending Clause 5.6/6.5 objection
not_decided.note: The Court did not decide the bill or the defective-meter dispute; the petitioner was left to press the objection claimed to have been filed on 2 March 2020 if still undecided.
